clue.text: State of dissolution in which things get very hot

definitions.text: State of dissolution in which things get very hot

parts.words: State of dissolution in which things get very hot
parts.note: a vessel where metals are heated until they liquefy and blend, also a figure for a society where cultures fuse

explanation.surface: A description of something breaking down while the temperature soars, like a chemistry lesson or a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dissolution' suggests decline or ending, but here it means things literally dissolving into one another in a hot crucible.
explanation.definitionFit: A crucible where substances fuse under heat, and by extension any mixture where separate elements dissolve together.

clue.text: As one dealing with people not well, I'd come out

definitions.text: one dealing with people not well

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who treats the sick says they have come out to help.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal word for a doctor, who treats the sick.

clue.text: Inner protections for ships

definitions.meaning: linings placed inside something to protect it, as in bin bags or helmet pads
large passenger vessels on a regular route

explanation.surface: Internal defences fitted to vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: Both protective inner layers and ocean-going passenger vessels.

clue.text: A purer boy doing wrong offers an apology

indicators.note: doing wrong suggests misbehaving letters, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: A well-behaved lad who slips up says sorry.
explanation.definitionFit: A polite phrase used to say sorry for an offence or interruption.

clue.text: Weed crushed under logs

indicators.note: crushed means squashed out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plant flattened beneath a pile of firewood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crushed' could give GROUND, but it is the anagram signal on 'under logs'.
explanation.definitionFit: A common yellow-flowered garden weed of the daisy family.

clue.text: Tramps heading off — they make a musical sound

indicators.note: heading off says the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: hoboes are tramps or vagrants

explanation.surface: Vagrants leaving town while playing a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodwind instruments with a double reed that play melodies.

clue.text: More than one great performer hurts when losing heart

indicators.note: losing its heart tells us the central letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: hurts in the sense of throbs with pain means aches

explanation.surface: A sad observation that star performers suffer when they lose their nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart' removes H, the middle letter of ACHES.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of a slang term for an expert or champion, someone outstanding at their skill.

clue.text: Country fellow providing delivery on cricket field

parts.note: China is a country
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A rural chap who supplies something on the cricket pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country fellow' reads as a rustic. In cricket, a chinaman is a left-arm wrist-spin ball turning into a right-hander.
explanation.definitionFit: A type of spin bowling ball, a delivery bowled in cricket.

clue.text: Disappointments with groups needing inner support

indicators.note: inner says the support word goes inside the groups word

parts.note: sets are groups
to back is to support

explanation.surface: Groups that are let down need emotional support.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverses or checks to progress, things that let one down.

clue.text: A building in which political opponents will get cross more than once

definitions.text: A building in which political opponents will get cross more than once

parts.words: A building in which political opponents will get cross more than once
parts.note: rival candidates are marked with an X by many voters on ballot papers in this place

explanation.surface: A venue where rival politicians keep losing their tempers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' means a mark X on a ballot paper, not angry.
explanation.definitionFit: The place where voters go to mark ballot papers for candidates at an election.

clue.text: Social ritual embraced by weird ancestors

indicators.note: embraced by says the word sits inside the run of letters of the following words

explanation.surface: An anthropological note about a ceremony practised by strange forebears.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball or ceilidh is a social occasion with set customs, a ritual of courtship and community.

clue.text: I got tools out as investigator of organ

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone getting their tools out, like a workman starting a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests a church instrument but means a body part, the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: An ear specialist, a doctor who studies that particular sense organ.

clue.text: To-do gets prisoner 'enry being locked up

indicators.note: being locked up puts the name inside the prisoner word

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prisoner
Henry without its H, as a Cockney says it, gives the familiar form 'Arry (Harry)

explanation.surface: A fuss because a Cockney inmate called Henry is being put behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H of ''enry' signals Cockney speech, so Henry's pet form Harry also loses its H: 'ARRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A fuss or commotion, a British colloquial synonym for a to-do.

clue.text: Ottoman ruler given a bit of food for his wife?

parts.note: the Ottoman emperor held the title sultan

explanation.surface: The sultan is handed a morsel to take to his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for his wife?' is a playful aside: the answer is also the title of a sultan's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: A dried seedless grape, a small item of food used in cakes.

clue.text: Cast doubt on earliest gospel? What is the point?

parts.note: to cast doubt on something is to question it
Mark is generally held to be the first gospel written

explanation.surface: A sceptic doubting the oldest gospel and asking what its purpose is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' means a punctuation mark, not a purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: The punctuation symbol ending an interrogative sentence, a 'point' in the old sense of punctuation sign.

clue.text: Well-established home, crumbling, finally came down

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the preceding word

parts.note: rain came down, it rained

explanation.surface: A long-standing house, falling apart, at last collapsed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'came down' suggests collapse but means rain fell.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep-rooted, firmly fixed in character or habit.

clue.text: Material engineers brought to Mediterranean area

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers of the British Army
the Levant is the eastern Mediterranean region

explanation.surface: Supplies brought by army engineers to the Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material' looks like a noun, cloth or supplies, but is the adjective meaning pertinent.
explanation.definitionFit: Material as an adjective means significant or pertinent to the matter in hand.

clue.text: One getting cold with little energy chooses items for mountaineering

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
C for cold, as on a tap
E is the symbol for energy
picks means chooses

explanation.surface: A climber who feels the cold and has little energy selects their gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Small axes used by climbers on frozen slopes.

clue.text: Police tag's so unreliable for one managing to break free

indicators.note: unreliable suggests letters not staying put, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An electronic police tag is so unreliable that an offender slips away.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer like Houdini whose act is escaping from chains, locks and boxes.

clue.text: River goes into sea, a place where yachts are seen

indicators.note: goes into means one piece is put inside another

parts.note: the main is an old word for the open sea

explanation.surface: A river flowing into the ocean, a scene with yachts.
explanation.definitionFit: A harbour or dock for pleasure boats and sailing craft.

clue.text: Abstainer surrounded by British booze? It's a struggle!

indicators.note: surrounded by means placed within another piece

parts.note: ale is beer, booze
TT, teetotal, describes someone who abstains from alcohol

explanation.surface: A teetotaller finds themselves amid British drink and finds it hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A fight or conflict, a hard contest.

clue.text: English politician to go wrong entertaining old ruler

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament

indicators.note: entertaining means holding a guest within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: to go wrong is to err

explanation.surface: An English politician strays while hosting a ruler from long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old' looks like part of 'old ruler' but supplies O inside ERR.
explanation.definitionFit: The supreme monarch of an empire, a sovereign ruler.

clue.text: Graduate has drink before 10

indicators.note: before places the drink in front of the graduate

parts.note: rum is an alcoholic drink
BA, Bachelor of Arts

explanation.surface: A graduate downs a drink ahead of ten o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' is not a time but a cross-reference to the answer at 10 across, a social ritual.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cuban ballroom form, an example of the activity in 10 across.

clue.text: Unfortunately inadequate couple of arts graduates in a state

indicators.note: inadequate means falling short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: alas is an exclamation meaning unfortunately
a Bachelor of Arts is a BA
a Master of Arts is an MA

explanation.surface: Two arts graduates find themselves sadly lacking and in a fluster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inadequate' trims ALAS to ALA. 'in a state' reads as being upset, but the definition is a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the southern United States, its capital Montgomery.

clue.text: TV presenter shows a knight meeting monarch getting excited

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight

indicators.note: getting excited means stirred up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A TV host shows a knight meeting an agitated king or queen.
explanation.definitionFit: The main newsreader or host who links a broadcast together.

clue.text: I had the thing to capture old fool

parts.note: I'd is the short form of I had

indicators.note: to capture means to hold inside, so a letter is put within the word

parts.note: it means the thing

explanation.surface: Someone admits they had the means to catch an old idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupid person, a simpleton or dolt.

clue.text: Match that might expose inadequacies

definitions.meaning: a ... match in cricket or rugby, an international fixture
an examination or trial reveals shortcomings

explanation.surface: A sports fixture that shows up a team's weaknesses.
explanation.definitionFit: An international fixture, and also an exam or trial designed to reveal weaknesses.

clue.text: Married woman may keep it — and demean man, I fancy

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or fanciful, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A wife's decision to keep something, and a speaker's whim to belittle a man.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname a woman had before marriage, which some keep rather than take the husband's.
